answer: Along the harbour, the old archive grants a licence only to a curator who has mounted an exhibition of relics verified by historians. The first licence needs one exhibition, the tenth ten, and the twentieth twenty, each from different relics with its own provenance file. Twenty invented curators would have to mount 210 verified exhibitions. Forging that breaks down because every relic is unique and publicly catalogued, so one piece cannot anchor two shows, and one forger cannot mount 210 collections at once, like a terrace of lamp rooms where every beacon needs its own keeper.
